title: Best Rewards Credit Cards 2026: 5 Compared for Points
description: Chase Sapphire Preferred, Amex Gold, Capital One Venture X, Citi Custom Cash, and Bilt Mastercard compared on rewards rates, annual fees, and real-world value.
lede: A rewards credit card can earn you hundreds of dollars in travel, cash back, or statement credits each year — but only if the card's earning structure matches how you actually spend. The $95 Chase Sapphire Preferred and the $0 Bilt Mastercard both made this list because they solve different problems. Annual fee is not a reliable proxy for value: the $395 Capital One Venture X consistently pays for itself for frequent travelers, while the $250 Amex Gold delivers outsized returns specifically for food and dining spending.

sections.heading: How to pick the right rewards card for your spending
paragraphs: Most people overestimate the importance of the sign-up bonus and underestimate the long-term earning structure. A 60,000-point sign-up bonus worth $750 is a one-time event; the ongoing multipliers on dining, travel, or groceries determine whether a card stays valuable for years.

subsections.heading: Annual fee math
paragraphs: Justify the annual fee before applying. The Amex Gold's $250 fee is offset by $120 in Uber Cash and $120 in dining credits annually — both in statement credit form — reducing the effective cost to $10 for someone who uses both. The Capital One Venture X's $395 fee includes a $300 annual travel credit and 10,000 anniversary bonus miles worth ~$100, making the net cost $0 or less for regular travelers. If you cannot use the credits the card offers, the fee is real.

subsections.heading: Earning rates and category match
paragraphs: Match the card's bonus categories to your top spending categories. The Amex Gold earns 4x at restaurants and U.S. supermarkets — if dining and groceries represent $2,000/month of your spend, that is 96,000 Membership Rewards points per year before the travel category. The Citi Custom Cash earns 5% cash back on your single highest spending category each month (up to $500/month), making it useful for focused spenders. The Chase Sapphire Preferred at 3x on dining and 2x on travel is the most balanced general travel card for moderate spenders.

subsections.heading: Redemption value: cents per point matters
paragraphs: Points are not created equal. Chase Ultimate Rewards points transferred to Hyatt or United can be worth 1.5–2.5 cents each. Amex Membership Rewards transferred to Air France/KLM Flying Blue can hit 2+ cents. Capital One miles transferred to Turkish Airlines Miles&Smiles for business class bookings can exceed 3 cents per mile. By contrast, redeeming any of these currencies for cash back or gift cards typically yields only 0.6–1 cent per point — a significant value destruction. The Citi Custom Cash and Bilt pay cash back or simple travel redemptions, which removes complexity but also caps upside.

subsections.heading: Foreign transaction fees and travel utility
paragraphs: None of the five cards here charge foreign transaction fees, which is the baseline expectation for any travel rewards card in 2026. The more meaningful differentiator is travel protections: the Chase Sapphire Preferred includes primary rental car insurance, trip cancellation/interruption coverage up to $10,000 per person, and baggage delay insurance. The Capital One Venture X adds cell phone protection and a Priority Pass lounge membership. Amex Gold's travel protections are weaker than either Chase card.

subsections.heading: No-annual-fee cards and the rent opportunity
paragraphs: The Citi Custom Cash and Bilt Mastercard both charge $0 annual fee. Bilt's standout feature is earning points on rent payments with no transaction fee — rent is typically your largest monthly expense and almost no other card rewards it. For renters spending $1,500–$2,500/month on rent, Bilt generates 1,500–2,500 points monthly from a category that otherwise earns nothing.

sections.heading: Bottom line
paragraphs: For most people who travel occasionally and spend heavily on dining, the Chase Sapphire Preferred at $95 per year remains the best single-card solution — strong multipliers, excellent travel protections, and a transfer partner network that rewards users who learn to optimize redemptions. The Amex Gold is worth the higher fee if dining and grocery spending is high enough to exhaust the credits.

The Capital One Venture X is the best premium card for frequent travelers who want simplicity — the lounge access and annual credits make it self-funding. The Citi Custom Cash and Bilt Mastercard solve specific problems: the Custom Cash is the best 5% card for focused category spenders, and Bilt is the only card that turns rent into points. Most cardholders would benefit from pairing one premium travel card with either Bilt (renters) or Citi Custom Cash (targeted cash back) rather than trying to cover every category with a single card.

faqs.q: Which rewards credit card has the best sign-up bonus in 2026?
faqs.a: Sign-up bonuses fluctuate, but the Chase Sapphire Preferred and Capital One Venture X have historically offered 60,000–75,000 point bonuses worth $750–$1,000+ when redeemed through travel portals. The Amex Gold frequently offers 60,000–90,000 Membership Rewards points. Always check the current public offer and any targeted offers before applying — the best bonus available changes monthly.

faqs.q: Is the Capital One Venture X worth $395 per year?
faqs.a: For travelers who fly at least once or twice per year, yes. The $300 annual travel credit (applied to any purchase through Capital One Travel), 10,000 anniversary bonus miles worth roughly $100, and Priority Pass lounge access together exceed the $395 fee. The effective net cost is $0 or less for someone who uses the travel portal credit each year. For infrequent travelers, the Chase Sapphire Preferred at $95 delivers better value.

faqs.q: Can you earn points on rent with a credit card?
faqs.a: The Bilt Mastercard is the primary card designed for this. It earns 1 point per dollar on rent paid through the Bilt app with no transaction fee, up to 100,000 points per year. Other cards can technically be used for rent if your landlord accepts credit cards, but payment processors typically charge 2.5–3% in fees — which eliminates any rewards value. Bilt's partnership with major landlords and property management companies eliminates that fee.

faqs.q: What is the Citi Custom Cash best used for?
faqs.a: The Citi Custom Cash earns 5% cash back on your single highest spending category each month, capped at $500 in that category. It works best for people with one dominant spending category — gas, groceries, dining, home improvement, or similar — who want a no-fee card that maximizes that specific spend. It earns 1% on everything else, so it pairs well as a secondary card alongside a flat-rate card for uncategorized spending.

faqs.q: Do any of these cards have foreign transaction fees?
faqs.a: None of the five cards in this comparison charge foreign transaction fees. Chase Sapphire Preferred, Amex Gold, Capital One Venture X, Citi Custom Cash, and Bilt Mastercard are all suitable for international use from a fee standpoint. The more relevant consideration abroad is acceptance: Visa and Mastercard have broader international acceptance than American Express, particularly at smaller merchants in Europe, Asia, and Latin America.

products.review: The Chase Sapphire Preferred earns 3x on dining and streaming, 2x on travel, and 1x everywhere else — with access to Chase's transfer partner network that includes Hyatt, United, British Airways, and Air France. Points are worth 1.25 cents each redeemed through Chase Travel, or up to 2.5 cents when transferred to Hyatt for peak-season hotel bookings. The $95 annual fee is offset by a $50 annual hotel credit through Chase Travel, making the effective cost $45 for most cardholders.
pros: 3x on dining and streaming, 2x on travel — balanced for moderate spenders
Transfer partners include Hyatt, United, British Airways — strong redemption upside
Primary rental car insurance and trip cancellation coverage up to $10,000/person
cons: 2x on general travel is lower than competitors like Venture X (2x) or Amex Gold (3x on flights)
$500/month dining cap does not apply but no grocery multiplier outside of select delivery apps

products.review: The Amex Gold's 4x Membership Rewards at restaurants and U.S. supermarkets is the highest multiplier in either category available on a mid-tier annual fee card. For a household spending $1,500/month on food combined, that is 72,000 points annually from those two categories alone. The $250 fee is partially offset by $120 Uber Cash (distributed monthly) and $120 in dining credits at participating restaurants including Grubhub and The Cheesecake Factory — net effective fee around $10 for users who exhaust both credits.
pros: 4x at restaurants worldwide and at U.S. supermarkets — unmatched at this fee level
$120 Uber Cash + $120 dining credits reduce effective annual fee to ~$10
Membership Rewards transfers to 21 airline and hotel programs including Delta and Hilton
cons: Credits require active use — Uber Cash is in $10 monthly increments, easy to forget
Weaker travel protections than Chase Sapphire Preferred; no primary rental car insurance

products.review: The Capital One Venture X earns 10x miles on hotels and rental cars booked through Capital One Travel, 5x on flights booked through the portal, and 2x on all other purchases. The $395 annual fee is front-loaded: the $300 travel credit (usable on any Capital One Travel booking) and 10,000 anniversary bonus miles (~$100 in travel) together exceed the fee. Priority Pass membership with unlimited guest access is included — unusually generous at this price tier.
pros: Unlimited Priority Pass lounge access with guest privileges included
$300 annual travel credit + 10,000 anniversary miles make the card self-funding
2x on all purchases — strong flat-rate floor with 5x–10x portal bonuses
cons: $395 annual fee requires active use of travel credit to justify — not for infrequent travelers
Capital One transfer partners are fewer than Chase or Amex; fewer premium airline options

products.review: The Citi Custom Cash automatically identifies your highest spending category each billing cycle and applies 5% cash back on up to $500 in that category — no category registration, no quarterly activation. It earns 1% on all other purchases. For someone whose top category is consistent (e.g., always groceries or always gas), this reliably delivers $25/month in cash back on the capped category. There is no annual fee and no complicated redemption structure.
pros: 5% on top spending category automatically — no enrollment or activation required
$0 annual fee with no earning cap on the 1% base rate
Simple cash back redemption — no points systems, transfer partners, or portal requirements
cons: 5% capped at $500/month in that category — high spenders in one category leave value on the table
1% on everything else is below competitive flat-rate cards; needs to be paired for full coverage

products.review: The Bilt Mastercard earns 1x point per dollar on rent paid through the Bilt app — with no processing fee, which is the card's defining feature. It also earns 3x on dining, 2x on travel, and 1x everywhere else, making the non-rent earning structure competitive with mid-tier travel cards. Bilt points transfer to American Airlines, United, Hyatt, and 10 other programs at 1:1 ratios. For renters paying $2,000/month, Bilt generates 24,000 points annually from rent alone — a category that otherwise earns nothing.
pros: 1x on rent with no transaction fee — the only card that meaningfully rewards rent payments
3x dining, 2x travel — competitive travel card structure on top of rent earnings
Transfers to AA, United, Hyatt, and others at 1:1; strong redemption potential
cons: Must make at least 5 purchases per statement period for rent points to post
$0 annual fee card with modest earning outside rent — less valuable for homeowners

methodology: Each card was evaluated on effective annual fee after credits, earning rates by spending category, transfer partner quality and breadth, travel protections, and practical value for three profiles: moderate spender, frequent diner, and frequent traveler.
pinDescription: Stop leaving points on the table — 5 best rewards credit cards in 2026 ranked by real value: Chase Sapphire Preferred, Amex Gold, Venture X, Citi Custom Cash, and Bilt for renters.
